title: Enforcement Decree of the Military Personnel Welfare Fund Act
full_text:
Enforcement Decree of the Military Personnel Welfare Fund Act

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Military Personnel Welfare Fund Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") and matters necessary for its implementation.

Article 2 (Operation of Welfare Facilities, Etc.)
(1) Revenue from the operation of military welfare facilities and sports facilities under Article 4 (1) 1 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "welfare facilities, etc.") shall be the total sales amount: Provided, That, in the case of consignment sales, only the commission may be treated as revenue. <Amended on November 23, 2011>
(2) Matters necessary for the operation of welfare facilities, etc., including their operating methods and eligible users, shall be prescribed by the Minister of National Defense. <Amended on November 23, 2011>

Article 3 (Uses of the Fund)
(1) Among the uses of the Military Personnel Welfare Fund under Article 3 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund"), support under Article 4 (2) 4 or 5 of the Act may be provided through an incorporated foundation established for scholarship programs for the children of military personnel and civilian military employees or an incorporated foundation established to support military research activities of military personnel in reserve service. In such cases, the relevant corporation shall prepare a business plan for each fiscal year and obtain approval from the Minister of National Defense. <Amended on November 23, 2011>
(2) "Projects necessary to boost the morale of military personnel, as prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4 (2) 3 of the Act means the following projects: <Amended on April 8, 2002; November 23, 2011; September 2, 2014>
1. Support and awards for sports and cultural events, events inviting military personnel in reserve service, and events promoting harmony between the military and civilians;
2. Encouragement and awards for military units, exemplary military personnel, etc.;
3. Encouragement and awards for military personnel serving in special areas, military personnel with meritorious service in operations, etc.;
4. Consolation for military personnel affected by disasters and bereaved families;
5. Support for the operation of facilities for the welfare of military personnel;
6. Support for employment-seeking activities;
7. Consolation and encouragement for the families of officers in long-term service, noncommissioned officers in long-term service, and warrant officers under Articles 6 and 7 of the Military Personnel Management Act.
(3) Deleted. <November 23, 2011>

Article 4 (Operation of the Student Loan Account)
(1) Student loans under Article 4-2 of the Act shall be provided to military personnel themselves and their children who fall under any of the following: <Amended on November 23, 2011>
1. Persons admitted to or enrolled in a school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act (excluding graduate schools);
2. Persons taking a course of study accredited pursuant to Article 3 of the Act on Recognition of Credits, Etc. to obtain recognition of an educational qualification under Article 8 of that Act.
(2) Student loans provided under paragraph (1) shall be repaid in installments over four years following a two-year grace period after the military personnel or their children who received the loans graduate from school (where a child graduates from a two-year college and transfers to a four-year university, after graduation from the four-year university): Provided, That the grace period and repayment period in any of the following cases shall be as prescribed by the Minister of National Defense. <Amended on December 30, 2000; November 23, 2011>
1. Where military personnel or their children who received the loans leave school before graduation;
2. Where the school from which military personnel or their children who received the loans graduate is a two-year college;
3. Where military personnel who received the loans are discharged or removed from the military register;
4. Where the repayment periods for student loans obtained for three or more children overlap.
(3) Deposits received from other accounts of the Military Personnel Welfare Fund under Article 4-2 (1) 3 of the Act may be used only where other financial resources of the student loan account are insufficient to finance student loans. <Newly Inserted on November 23, 2011>
(4) The interest rate (including the overdue interest rate), maximum amount, repayment procedures, and other matters necessary for student loans under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by the Minister of National Defense following consultation with the relevant institutions. <Amended on November 23, 2011>

Article 5 (Operation of the Housing Support Account)
Deposits received from other accounts of the Military Personnel Welfare Fund under Article 4-3 (1) 5 of the Act may be used only where other financial resources of the housing support account are insufficient to cover support for funds to rent private housing. <Amended on October 15, 2019>

Article 6 Deleted. <December 30, 2002>

Article 7 (Acting and Deputized Accounting Officers)
(1) The Minister of National Defense may appoint acting or deputized public officials in the Ministry of National Defense and each armed service to perform all duties on behalf of, or share part of the duties of, the Fund revenue collection officer, Fund finance officer, Fund expenditure officer, and Fund cash officer. <Amended on December 30, 2002>
(2) Authority to appoint acting or deputized public officials for each armed service under paragraph (1) shall be delegated to the chief of staff of the respective armed service.
(3) Deleted. <December 30, 2002>
(4) The appointment of an acting or deputized public official under paragraphs (1) and (2) may be replaced by designation by the Minister of National Defense or the chief of staff of the relevant armed service of a position established in an office under his or her jurisdiction.

Article 8 Deleted. <December 30, 2002>

Article 9 (Methods of Receiving Fund Revenue)
(1) No person other than a Fund cash officer may receive revenue of the Fund: Provided, That this shall not apply where a person designated by the Minister of National Defense or the Bank of Korea is entrusted with receiving such revenue.
(2) When a Fund cash officer or a person designated by the Minister of National Defense under paragraph (1) receives revenue of the Fund, the officer or person shall pay the amount received into the Military Personnel Welfare Fund account at the Bank of Korea without delay.

Article 10 (Allocation of Ceilings for Acts Giving Rise to Expenditure of the Fund)
(1) The Minister of National Defense shall allocate to each Fund finance officer a ceiling for acts giving rise to expenditure within the scope of the Fund management plan. <Amended on December 30, 2002>
(2) When allocating a ceiling for acts giving rise to expenditure pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister of National Defense shall notify the relevant Fund expenditure officer and the Bank of Korea thereof. <Amended on December 30, 2002>
(3) A Fund finance officer shall not undertake acts giving rise to expenditure in excess of the ceiling allocated under paragraph (1). <Amended on December 30, 2002>

Article 11 (Procedures for Expenditure of the Fund)
(1) When intending to disburse the Fund, a Fund finance officer shall forward documents relating to acts giving rise to expenditure to the Fund expenditure officer. <Amended on December 30, 2002>
(2) Deleted. <December 30, 2002>

Article 12 (Management of Surplus Funds)
(1) Where the Fund has surplus funds, the Minister of National Defense may manage them by the following methods: <Amended on April 8, 2002; July 29, 2008; November 15, 2010>
1. Deposits with banks under the Banking Act;
2. Deposits with collective investment business entities, trust business entities, and merchant banks under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act;
3. Deleted. <July 29, 2008>
4. Deposits with postal authorities under the Postal Savings and Insurance Act;
5. Purchase of securities under Article 4 of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act;
6. Transactions in exchange-traded derivatives under Article 5 (2) of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act.
(2) Where a Fund cash officer intends to deposit funds, the officer shall open a deposit account at a financial institution under paragraph (1) and make the deposit into that account.

Article 13 (Establishment of Accounts)
The Minister of National Defense may establish separate accounts for the Ministry of National Defense and each armed service within the Military Personnel Welfare Fund account established at the Bank of Korea pursuant to Article 10 of the Act.

Article 14 (Processing of Unique Identifying Information)
The Minister of National Defense may process data containing resident registration numbers under Article 19, subparagraph 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act where it is unavoidable for performing the following affairs: <Amended on October 15, 2019>
1. Affairs concerning the payment of consolation money to military personnel affected by disasters and bereaved families under Article 4(2)3 of the Act and Article 3(2)4 of this Decree;
2. Affairs concerning support for scholarship programs for the children of military personnel and civilian employees of the military under Article 4(2)4 of the Act;
3. Affairs concerning student loans to military personnel themselves and their children under Article 4-2(2) of the Act;
4. Affairs concerning support for funds for renting private housing for military officers and noncommissioned officers under Article 4-3(2) of the Act.

Article 15 Deleted. <December 30, 2002>

Article 16 Deleted. <December 30, 2002>

Article 17 (Regulations on the Management and Operation of the Fund)
Detailed matters necessary for the enforcement of this Decree shall be prescribed by the Minister of National Defense.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 15122, July 16, 1996>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Procedures for Vesting of the Fund)
The procedures for vesting of the Fund under Article 2 of the Addenda to the Act shall be prescribed by the Minister of National Defense.

Article 3 (Transfer from Military Personnel Pensions)
(1) The funds for loan programs for military personnel as of June 30, 1996 to which the Fund succeeds in their entirety pursuant to Article 3 of the Addenda to the Act mean the funds remaining after deducting the amounts disbursed through June 30, 1996 from the funds earmarked for loan programs in the 1996 Military Personnel Pension Fund Operation Plan, and the associated claims and liabilities mean all loan receivables and liabilities held by the Military Personnel Pension Fund as of June 30, 1996.
(2) The specific procedures for succession to the funds for loan programs for military personnel and the associated claims and liabilities under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by the Minister of National Defense.

Article 4 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
The Enforcement Decree of the Military Personnel Pension Special Account Act shall be amended as follows:
Articles 7-2 and 7-3 and Article 7-4(2) and (3) shall each be deleted.

ADDENDA (Enforcement Decree of the Postal Insurance Special Account Act) <Presidential Decree No. 16762, March 28, 2000>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) and (2) Omitted.
(3) The Enforcement Decree of the Military Personnel Welfare Fund Act shall be amended as follows:
In Article 12(1)5, "Communications Deposits and Insurance Act" shall be replaced by "Postal Savings and Insurance Act".
(4) through (16) Omitted.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 17100, December 30, 2000>

(1) (Enforcement Date) This Decree shall enter into force on January 1, 2001.
(2) (Transitional Measures Concerning Repayment of Student Loans from the National Treasury) The amended provisions of Article 4 shall also apply to persons who obtained student loans from the National Treasury before this Decree enters into force and have not completed repayment.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 17571, April 8, 2002>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA (Enforcement Decree of the Management of the National Funds Act) <Presidential Decree No. 17824, December 30, 2002>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on January 1, 2003. <Proviso omitted>

Articles 2 through 4 Omitted.

Article 5 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) through (26) Omitted.
(27) The Enforcement Decree of the Military Personnel Welfare Fund Act shall be amended as follows:
Article 6 shall be deleted.
In Article 7(1), each occurrence of "Fund cash management authorizing officer and Fund cash officer" shall be replaced by "Fund revenue collection officer, Fund finance officer, Fund expenditure officer, and Fund cash officer", and paragraph (3) of the same Article shall be deleted.
Article 8 shall be deleted.
In Article 10(1) and (3), "Fund cash management authorizing officer" shall be replaced in each instance by "Fund finance officer", and in paragraph (2) of the same Article, "Fund cash officer" shall be replaced by "Fund expenditure officer".
In Article 11(1), "Fund cash management authorizing officer" shall be replaced by "Fund finance officer" and "Fund cash officer" shall be replaced by "Fund expenditure officer", and paragraph (2) of the same Article shall be deleted.
Articles 14 through 16 shall each be deleted.
(28) Omitted.

Article 6 Omitted.

ADDENDA (Enforcement Decree of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act) <Presidential Decree No. 20947, July 29, 2008>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on February 4, 2009. <Proviso omitted>

Articles 2 through 25 Omitted.

Article 26 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) through (24) Omitted.
(25) The Enforcement Decree of the Military Personnel Welfare Fund Act shall be partially amended as follows:
Article 12(1)2 shall be amended as follows; subparagraph 3 of the same paragraph shall be deleted; in subparagraph 5 of the same paragraph, "securities under Article 2(1) of the Securities and Exchange Act" shall be replaced by "securities under Article 4 of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act"; and subparagraph 6 of the same paragraph shall be amended as follows:
2. Deposits with collective investment business entities, trust business entities, and merchant banks under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act;
6. Trading in exchange-traded derivatives under Article 5(2) of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act.
(26) through (113) Omitted.

Articles 27 and 28 Omitted.

ADDENDA (Enforcement Decree of the Banking Act) <Presidential Decree No. 22493, November 15, 2010>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on November 18, 2010.

Articles 2 and 3 Omitted.

Article 4 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) through (26) Omitted.
(27) The Enforcement Decree of the Military Personnel Welfare Fund Act shall be partially amended as follows:
In Article 12(1)1, "financial institutions" shall be replaced by "banks".
(28) through (115) Omitted.

Article 5 Omitted.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 23306, November 23, 2011>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on November 25, 2011.

Article 2 (Applicability to Repayment of Student Loans)
The amended provisions of Article 4(2)4 shall also apply where a student loan has been obtained under the former provisions and repayment has not been completed as of the time this Decree enters into force.

ADDENDA (Decree Partially Amending the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions and Other Decrees to Establish a Legal Basis for the Processing of Sensitive Information and Unique Identifying Information) <Presidential Decree No. 25532, August 6, 2014>

This Decree shall enter into force on August 7, 2014.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 25584, September 2, 2014>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 30122, October 15, 2019>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
